Visible_Tongue_Signs: Pink, moist tongue with normal papillae distribution, no swelling, discoloration, or lesions

Key_Symptoms: Sore, smooth tongue, burning sensation, difficulty swallowing, fatigue
Visible_Tongue_Signs: Smooth, pale, atrophic tongue surface with loss of papillae (atrophic glossitis)
Common_Systemic_Symptoms: Fatigue, pallor, dizziness, koilonychia (spoon nails), restless legs, hair thinning
Risk_Factors: Heavy menstrual bleeding, poor dietary iron intake, pregnancy, chronic blood loss, GI disorders

Key_Symptoms: Burning, sore tongue, beefy red appearance, taste changes
Visible_Tongue_Signs: Beefy red, smooth, swollen tongue with loss of papillae (Hunter glossitis) - classic sign of B12 deficiency
Common_Systemic_Symptoms: Megaloblastic anemia, peripheral neuropathy (numbness/tingling), memory issues, pale skin
Risk_Factors: Vegan/vegetarian diet, pernicious anemia, gastric bypass surgery, elderly age, metformin use, malabsorption

Key_Symptoms: Sore, smooth tongue, burning sensation, difficulty swallowing
Visible_Tongue_Signs: Smooth, pale-to-red atrophic tongue surface with papillae loss
Common_Systemic_Symptoms: Megaloblastic anemia, peripheral neuropathy, fatigue, pale skin, memory issues
Risk_Factors: Vegan/vegetarian diet, pernicious anemia, gastric bypass surgery, elderly age, metformin use, malabsorption

Key_Symptoms: Sore red tongue, burning sensation, fatigue, weakness
Visible_Tongue_Signs: Beefy red, smooth, swollen tongue surface with papillae atrophy
Common_Systemic_Symptoms: Megaloblastic anemia symptoms: fatigue, pallor, irritability, poor concentration, shortness of breath
Risk_Factors: Poor dietary intake of leafy greens/legumes, alcoholism, pregnancy, malabsorption, certain medications (methotrexate)

Key_Symptoms: Sore purplish tongue, burning sensation, cracked lips
Visible_Tongue_Signs: Magenta (purplish-red) discoloration of tongue with papillary atrophy
Common_Systemic_Symptoms: Angular cheilitis, sore throat, seborrheic dermatitis around nose, eye irritation/light sensitivity
Risk_Factors: Poor dietary intake of dairy/eggs/meat/leafy greens, alcoholism, malabsorption, prolonged restrictive diets

Key_Symptoms: Sore, swollen, bright red tongue, difficulty eating, burning pain
Visible_Tongue_Signs: Bright red, swollen, inflamed tongue, sometimes with ulceration at edges
Common_Systemic_Symptoms: Classic triad: dermatitis, diarrhea, dementia (pellagra); angular stomatitis, fatigue
Risk_Factors: Corn-based diet without niacin fortification, alcoholism, carcinoid syndrome, isoniazid therapy, malabsorption

Key_Symptoms: Sore tongue, dryness, altered taste, mouth discomfort
Visible_Tongue_Signs: Dry, inflamed tongue surface with reduced papillae, general oral dryness
Common_Systemic_Symptoms: Night blindness, dry skin (phrynoderma), dry eyes, reduced immunity
Risk_Factors: Vitamin A deficient diet, fat malabsorption, alcoholism, liver disease

Key_Symptoms: Sore tongue, altered/reduced taste sensation, delayed wound healing
Visible_Tongue_Signs: Inflamed, sometimes fissured tongue surface with variable papillae changes, oral mucosal irritation
Common_Systemic_Symptoms: Acrodermatitis enteropathica-like rash, diarrhea, impaired immunity, poor appetite, hair loss
Risk_Factors: Malabsorption syndromes, vegetarian/vegan diet, chronic diarrhea, alcoholism, pregnancy

Key_Symptoms: Map-like patches on tongue that change location/shape over time, mild burning with certain foods
Visible_Tongue_Signs: Irregular, smooth, red patches with white/yellow raised borders giving a map-like appearance, patterns migrate over days to weeks
Common_Systemic_Symptoms: Generally benign and asymptomatic; occasional association with psoriasis or atopic conditions
Risk_Factors: Family history, psoriasis association, stress, hormonal changes, generally idiopathic

Key_Symptoms: Visible grooves/cracks on tongue surface, occasional mild discomfort with spicy foods, food trapping in fissures
Visible_Tongue_Signs: Deep grooves or fissures across the dorsal tongue surface, normal pink coloration between fissures
Common_Systemic_Symptoms: Generally asymptomatic; may coexist with geographic tongue
Risk_Factors: Genetic/developmental trait, aging, association with certain syndromes (e.g., Melkersson-Rosenthal), generally benign

Key_Symptoms: Burning mouth sensation, altered taste, soreness, white patches that can be scraped off
Visible_Tongue_Signs: White/cream-colored plaques on tongue and oral mucosa, erythema underneath when plaques are removed
Common_Systemic_Symptoms: May coexist with underlying immunosuppression, diabetes, or recent antibiotic use
Risk_Factors: Denture wearers, immunosuppression, diabetes, antibiotic/corticosteroid use, dry mouth, infancy or old age

Key_Symptoms: Visible dark/discolored fuzzy coating on tongue, mild bad breath, altered taste
Visible_Tongue_Signs: Elongated filiform papillae giving a hairy appearance, often with black, brown, or yellow discoloration from bacterial/food staining
Risk_Factors: Poor oral hygiene, smoking, antibiotic use, dehydration, soft diet lacking abrasive food contact

Key_Symptoms: Usually asymptomatic, occasional mild soreness or burning at central tongue area
Visible_Tongue_Signs: Smooth, well-demarcated, rhomboid (diamond)-shaped red patch at the midline posterior dorsal tongue, devoid of papillae
Common_Systemic_Symptoms: Often associated with chronic Candida colonization; generally no other systemic symptoms
Risk_Factors: Denture wearers, smoking, immunosuppression, chronic candidal infection, diabetes

Key_Symptoms: White patch that cannot be scraped off, usually painless, occasional roughness sensation
Visible_Tongue_Signs: Well-defined white or grayish-white patch/plaque on tongue surface that does not rub off, surface may be smooth or slightly thickened
Common_Systemic_Symptoms: Generally localized; possible association with chronic irritation history
Risk_Factors: Tobacco use (smoking/chewing), chronic alcohol use, chronic mechanical irritation, HPV association in some cases
